census-surname-help.output:
Usage: cli estimate census-surname [OPTIONS] INPUT_FILE

  Estimate race/ethnicity using Census LSTM model.

  Uses LSTM neural networks trained on U.S. Census data to predict
  race/ethnicity probabilities from last names.

  Examples:

      # Basic estimate
      ethnicolr estimate census-surname data.csv -l surname

      # With MC-dropout ranges
      ethnicolr estimate census-surname data.csv -l surname -u 0.95 -m 200

      # Specify output file and Census year
      ethnicolr estimate census-surname data.csv -l surname -o results.csv -y 2000

Options:
  -l, --last-column TEXT          Column name containing last names  [required]
  -o, --output PATH               Output CSV file (default: census-
                                  estimates.csv)
  -y, --year [2000|2010|2020]     Census year for model  [default: 2020]
  -u, --uncertainty-level FLOAT RANGE
                                  MC-dropout range level (0.0-1.0)  [0.0<x<1.0]
  -m, --mc-iterations INTEGER RANGE
                                  Monte Carlo iterations for MC-dropout ranges
                                  [default: 100; 10<=x<=1000]
  --overwrite                     Overwrite output file if it exists
  --help                          Show this message and exit.

florida-voter-surname-help.output:
Usage: cli estimate florida-voter-surname [OPTIONS] INPUT_FILE

  Estimate race/ethnicity using Florida voter registration LSTM model.

  Uses LSTM neural networks trained on Florida voter registration data to
  predict race/ethnicity probabilities from last names. Estimates 5 categories:
  asian, hispanic, nh_black, nh_white, other.

  Examples:

      # Basic estimate
      ethnicolr estimate florida-voter-surname data.csv -l surname

      # With MC-dropout ranges
      ethnicolr estimate florida-voter-surname data.csv -l surname -u 0.95 -m 200

      # Specify output file
      ethnicolr estimate florida-voter-surname data.csv -l surname -o results.csv

Options:
  -l, --last-column TEXT          Column name containing last names  [required]
  -o, --output PATH               Output CSV file (default: florida-
                                  estimates.csv)
  -u, --uncertainty-level FLOAT RANGE
                                  MC-dropout range level (0.0-1.0)  [0.0<x<1.0]
  -m, --mc-iterations INTEGER RANGE
                                  Monte Carlo iterations for MC-dropout ranges
                                  [default: 100; 10<=x<=1000]
  --overwrite                     Overwrite output file if it exists
  --help                          Show this message and exit.

wikipedia-surname-help.output:
Usage: cli estimate wikipedia-surname [OPTIONS] INPUT_FILE

  Estimate race/ethnicity using Wikipedia LSTM model.

  Uses LSTM neural networks trained on Wikipedia person data to predict detailed
  ethnic categories from last names. Provides 13 ethnic categories with
  hierarchical naming (e.g., "GreaterEuropean,WestEuropean,Germanic").

  Examples:

      # Basic estimate
      ethnicolr estimate wikipedia-surname data.csv -l surname

      # With MC-dropout ranges
      ethnicolr estimate wikipedia-surname data.csv -l surname -u 0.95 -m 200

      # Specify output file
      ethnicolr estimate wikipedia-surname data.csv -l surname -o results.csv

Options:
  -l, --last-column TEXT          Column name containing last names  [required]
  -o, --output PATH               Output CSV file (default: wiki-estimates.csv)
  -u, --uncertainty-level FLOAT RANGE
                                  MC-dropout range level (0.0-1.0)  [0.0<x<1.0]
  -m, --mc-iterations INTEGER RANGE
                                  Monte Carlo iterations for MC-dropout ranges
                                  [default: 100; 10<=x<=1000]
  --overwrite                     Overwrite output file if it exists
  --help                          Show this message and exit.
